title.narrative: Provision of life-saving WASH assistance to the most vulnerable communities in Baladweyn district to address the impact

description.narrative: ltpgtPuntland Minority Women Development Organization (PMWDO) proposes to scale up its WASH activities in Baladweyn district with an immediate life-saving response to address the urgent needs of communities facing famine risks, particularly as Somalia struggles to recover from the 2020-2023 drought and recent flooding, while potentially moving towards another multi-season drought, as outlined in the 2025 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP). The project aims to provide WASH services to up to 10,000 people across 4 IDP settlements and 2 host community villages, including Guudlaawe, Bilis diid, shabelle , Kunaso cadeley and hiran billa. Key interventions will include emthe extension of piping networks to a borehole in Baladweyn village, serving multiple IDP settlements. The project will also construct 4 water kiosks to facilitate water distribution and coordination. Additionally, PMWDO will implement water treatment measures, including the provision of aqua tabs and chlorination of communal water sources in AWD/Cholera hotspots. In the 4 IDP settlements, 54 emergency latrines will be installed, with 15% designed to be accessible for persons with disabilities (PwDs). Mass hygiene promotion campaigns will target all settlements, educating the community on preventive measures against water-related diseases. Hygiene kits, including standard menstrual hygiene management (MHM) sets, will be distributed to 1000 households, particularly benefiting pregnant and lactating mothers and children with malnutrition. Furthermore, 22 sets of sanitation tools will be provided to support solid waste management and cleanup efforts in the targeted areas. This comprehensive WASH response, addressing the challenges identified in the HNRP such as inadequate access to safe water and suitable living space, will operate over six months, directly benefiting vulnerable populations in Baladweyn as they cope with severe drought conditions and associated health risks. Reports indicate that millions across Somalia require urgent assistance, underscoring the critical need for this integrated emergency response to prevent further deterioration of health and sanitation in affected areas.lt/pgt
